title: Alert Orchestra: multi-signal early-warning ensemble + adaptive escalation windows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a resilient, multi-signal early-warning layer that fuses traces, metrics, and enriched logs to reduce false-positive burn-rate alerts and implement adaptive escalation windows. The goal is to detect emerging SLO violations earlier with higher precision and automate paging behavior based on signal confidence, customer tier, and time-of-day. This work touches tracing hooks (capture request metadata + queue/dispatch timings), metrics/log ingestion (new enrichment fields and fast path for high-cardinality routes), anomaly detector model and alert rules, and on-call escalation policy configuration in PagerDuty/Console.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing SDK adds two new mandatory fields: request_priority and scheduler_queue_ms and these fields are present in >=95% of sampled spans for supported services
Realtime metrics pipeline emits per-route p50/p95/p99 and error-rate micro-buckets at 10s resolution for top 200 routes
Anomaly ensemble (metric thresholds + trace spike + log-error-signature) achieves at least 25% reduction in burn-rate alert false positives on last 3 months of historical data in staging
Alert engine supports 'escalation window' configuration by customer tier and weekday/hour and the Console exposes controls to preview effective paging window
PagerDuty integration creates deduplicated incidents when ensemble confidence >= 0.9 and routes to the correct escalation policy based on team + severity
Runbook links and automated first-response hints appear in alerts for top 10 most common error signatures
tasks: Design trace hook schema and backward-compatibility plan
Implement trace hook in internal tracing SDK (go/python/node) and add CI lint for new fields
Add vector/ingest enrichment to attach model_variant, request_priority, and experiment flags to logs and metrics
Add a high-throughput aggregator path for high-cardinality routes in metrics pipeline
Prototype ensemble anomaly detector (lightweight rules + isolation forest) and offline evaluation against 3 months of production telemetry
Author new alert rules and burn-rate gating logic in Alert Orchestrator
Add escalation window UI and backend enforcement in Console and link to PagerDuty policies
QA + synthetic traffic test, runbook validation, canary rollout to 10% of traffic, and metricized rollback plan
notes: Rationale: current burn-rate alerts are noisy during region-wide reconf and model rollouts; coupling trace-level signals and log error signatures should provide better attribution and reduce paging churn.
We must be careful with cardinality — avoid attaching freeform user IDs to metrics; use route/service/variant buckets.
Escalation windows are additive to existing SLO paging policies — they must never silence Sev-1 during active incidents, only modulate low-confidence pages.
Consider adding a synthetic golden prompt probe per major route to detect model regressions ahead of traffic anomalies. This will be tracked as follow-up if prototype shows value.
